narrative:
The model estimates a 28% chance that you will not pass your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

Three factors stood out most in the prediction. First, your record shows no past class failures, which the model sees as a positive sign that actually pulls your chances toward passing. However, this helpful factor was outweighed by two others that pushed the prediction toward failing.

Your father’s education level, which is primary school only, was the strongest influence pointing to a higher risk of failure. Among students who passed, far fewer had fathers with only primary education, so the model associates this background with greater academic difficulty. The second most important factor was your reason for choosing this school—living close to it. While many students pick the school for its course offerings or reputation, your choice based on proximity worked against you in the prediction, possibly because the model links it to less deliberate academic planning.

To improve, focus on building stronger study habits. You currently study less than two hours per week, while most students who succeed spend two to five hours or more. Increasing your weekly study time, seeking extra support at school, and making fuller use of your desire to pursue higher education could meaningfully raise your chances of passing.
